title: Dijkstra: shortest paths II
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: What vertex does Dijkstra settle next?
questions.answer: The unsettled vertex with the smallest current tentative distance.

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: predecessor table — For each vertex, stores the prior vertex on its best-known path.
relaxation — Replace a distance when a cheaper route is discovered.
settled — Shortest distance is final for a vertex under non-negative edge weights.
infinity — Marker for an as-yet unreachable vertex.
route reconstruction — Follow predecessor links backwards then reverse.

blocks.title: Track improvements
blocks.text: Relax each edge by comparing the candidate total with the current best-known distance.

blocks.title: Remember predecessors
blocks.text: When a distance improves, store the vertex from which the improvement came.

blocks.title: Finish with the best distance
blocks.text: Here E reaches distance 7 after A, C, B and D have settled.

blocks.title: Reconstruct backwards
blocks.text: Follow E←D←B←C←A, then reverse it to get the forward route.
